# 1. Introduction

This report examines alternative factor structures for trust in science and scientists using confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and structural equation modeling (SEM).

The following models are examined:

1. Unidimensional CFA model
2. Simple-structure two-factor CFA model
3. Second-order CFA model
4. Bifactor CFA model
5. Bifactor SEM predicting belief in information
6. Bifactor SEM predicting trust in individual scientists

# 2. Data preparation

## 2.1. Load packages

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(lavaan)
library(qgraph)
library(semPlot)
library(haven)
library(semTools)
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
```

## 2.2. Import the dataset

```{r import-data}
Data_Trust <- read_excel("TSModeling_Dataset.xlsx")

# Inspect the dataset
dim(Data_Trust)
names(Data_Trust)
head(Data_Trust)
```

## 2.3. Reverse-code items
The following items are reverse-coded using the transformation `6 - x`, assuming a five-point response scale ranging from 1 to 5.

```{r reverse-coding}
reverse_cols <- c(
  "ts1", "ts2", "ts3", "ts4", "ts6", "ts8",
  "ts13", "ts17", "ts18", "ts19", "ts20", "ts21"
)

Data_Trust[, reverse_cols] <-
  6 - Data_Trust[, reverse_cols]
```

# 3. Confirmatory factor analysis

## 3.1. Unidimensional CFA model

The unidimensional model specifies a single latent factor, `TrustinScienceScientist`, measured by all 21 observed items.

```{r cfa-unidimensional}
Model_Uni<-'TrustinScienceScientist =~ ts1 + ts2 + ts3 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7
                                     + ts8 + ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts12 + ts13
                                     +ts14 + ts15 + ts16 + ts17 + ts18 +ts19 + ts20 + ts21'
FitUni <- cfa(Model_Uni, data = Data_Trust, std.lv = TRUE)
summary(FitUni,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE)
modindices(FitUni)

```

## 3.2. Simple-structure two-factor CFA model

The two-factor model distinguishes between trust in science and trust in scientists.

- `TrustinScience` is measured by five items.
- `TrustinScientist` is measured by 16 items.

```{r cfa-simple-structure}
Model_Simple<-'TrustinScience =~ ts3 + ts12 + ts14 + ts15 + ts21
            TrustinScientist =~ ts1 + ts2 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7 + ts8 + ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts13 + ts16 + ts17 + ts18 + ts19 + ts20 '
FitSimple <- cfa(Model_Simple, data = Data_Trust)
summary(FitSimple,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE)
modindices(FitSimple)
```

## 3.3. Second-order CFA model

The second-order model specifies a general trust factor, `TrustGeneral`, underlying the two first-order factors.

```{r cfa-second-order}
Model_SecondOrder <- '
  TrustinScience =~ ts3 + ts12 + ts14 + ts15 + ts21 
  TrustinScientist =~ ts1 + ts2 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7 + ts8 + ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts13 + ts16 + ts17 + ts18 + ts19 + ts20 
  TrustGeneral =~ TrustinScience + TrustinScientist'
Fit_SecondOrder<- cfa(Model_SecondOrder, data = Data_Trust)
summary(Fit_SecondOrder,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE)
modindices(Fit_SecondOrder)
```

### 3.3.1. Constrained second-order model

The unconstrained second-order model may encounter identification problems or negative latent residual variances. The following version fixes the variance of the higher-order factor to 1 and fixes both first-order latent residual variances to 0.05.

```{r cfa-second-order-constrained}
Model_SecondOrder <- '
  TrustinScience =~ ts3 + ts12 + ts14 + ts15 + ts21 
  TrustinScientist =~ ts1 + ts2 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7 + ts8 + ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts13 + ts16 + ts17 + ts18 + ts19 + ts20 
  TrustGeneral =~ TrustinScience + TrustinScientist
  
  #Fixed variance of higher-order factor
  TrustGeneral~~1*TrustGeneral
  
  #Ensured positiive residual variances
  TrustinScience~~ 0.05*TrustinScience
  TrustinScientist~~ 0.05*TrustinScientist
'
Fit_SecondOrder<- cfa(Model_SecondOrder, data = Data_Trust)
summary(Fit_SecondOrder,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE)
modindices(Fit_SecondOrder)
```

## 3.4. Bifactor CFA model

The bifactor model specifies a general trust factor loading on all 21 items and two specific factors representing trust in science and trust in scientists.

The general factor and the two specific factors are constrained to be mutually orthogonal.

```{r cfa-bifactor}
Model_Bi<-'TrustinScienceScientist =~ ts1 + ts2 + ts3 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7 + ts8 + ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts12 + ts13 + ts14 + ts15 + ts16 + ts17 + ts18 + ts19 + ts20 + ts21
           TrustinScience =~ ts3 + ts12 + ts14 + ts15 + ts21
           TrustinScientist =~ ts1 + ts2 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7 + ts8 + ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts13 + ts16 + ts17 + ts18 + ts19 + ts20
           TrustinScienceScientist ~~ 0*TrustinScience
           TrustinScienceScientist ~~ 0*TrustinScientist
           TrustinScience ~~ 0*TrustinScientist'
FitBi <- cfa(Model_Bi, data = Data_Trust)
summary(FitBi,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE)
modindices(FitBi)
```

## 3.5. Factor loadings for four CFA models
```{r}
extract_loadings <- function(fit, model_name) {

  standardizedSolution(fit, ci = TRUE) %>%
    filter(op == "=~") %>%
    transmute(
      Model = model_name,
      Factor = lhs,
      Item = rhs,
      Std_Loading = est.std,
      SE = se,
      CI_Lower = ci.lower,
      CI_Upper = ci.upper,
      p_value = pvalue
    )
}

All_Loadings <- bind_rows(
  extract_loadings(FitUni, "Unidimensional"),
  extract_loadings(FitSimple, "Simple structure"),
  extract_loadings(Fit_SecondOrder, "Second-order"),
  extract_loadings(FitBi, "Bifactor")
)

print(All_Loadings, n = Inf)

write.csv(
  All_Loadings,
  "All_CFA_Standardized_Loadings.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
# 4. Structural equation modeling

## 4.1. Bifactor SEM predicting belief in information

This model examines whether the general trust factor and the two specific trust factors predict `Outcome_beliefinfo`.

```{r sem-bifactor-belief-information}
Model_Bi1<-'TrustinScienceScientist =~ ts1 + ts2 + ts3 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7 + ts8 + ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts12 + ts13 + ts14 + ts15 + ts16 + ts17 + ts18 + ts19 + ts20 + ts21
           TrustinScience =~ ts3 + ts12 + ts14 + ts15 + ts21
           TrustinScientist =~ ts1 + ts2 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7 + ts8 + ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts13 + ts16 + ts17 + ts18 + ts19 + ts20
            TrustinScienceScientist ~ 0*TrustinScience + 0*TrustinScientist
            Outcome_beliefinfo ~ TrustinScience + TrustinScientist + TrustinScienceScientist'
SEMBi1 <- sem(Model_Bi1, data = Data_Trust, std.lv = TRUE)
summary(SEMBi1,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE)
```

## 4.2. Bifactor SEM predicting trust in individual scientists

This model examines whether the general trust factor and the two specific trust factors predict `Outcome_highcred`.

```{r sem-bifactor-individual-scientists}
Model_Bi2<-'TrustinScienceScientist =~ ts1 + ts2 + ts3 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7 + ts8 + ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts12 + ts13 + ts14 + ts15 + ts16 + ts17 + ts18 + ts19 + ts20 + ts21
           TrustinScience =~ ts3 + ts12 + ts14 + ts15 + ts21
           TrustinScientist =~ ts1 + ts2 + ts4 + ts5 + ts6 + ts7 + ts8 + ts9 + ts10 + ts11 + ts13 + ts16 + ts17 + ts18 + ts19 + ts20
            TrustinScienceScientist ~ 0*TrustinScience + 0*TrustinScientist
           Outcome_highcred ~ TrustinScience + TrustinScientist + TrustinScienceScientist'
SEMBi2 <- sem(Model_Bi2, data = Data_Trust, std.lv = TRUE)
summary(SEMBi2,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE)
```
